# Godot PolyForge — agent instructions

PolyForge is a Godot 4 development-time asset compiler. Geometry is authored in GDScript,
validated, previewed, and exported as ordinary GLB files. The addon does not need to ship
with the game that consumes those files.

## Build an asset

Read `examples/bronze_guardian_recipe.gd`, then create a project-owned recipe with:

```gdscript
extends RefCounted
const Assembly := preload("res://addons/polyforge/core/assembly.gd")
const Parameters := preload("res://addons/polyforge/core/parameters.gd")
const Stock := preload("res://addons/polyforge/core/stock.gd")

func parameters() -> Dictionary:
	return {"height": Parameters.scale(1.0, 0.5, 2.0, "m", "Canonical height")}

func build(p) -> Dictionary:
	var height := p.value("height")
	var asset := Assembly.new()
	# asset.add("semantic_name", mesh, transform, {"tags": [...]})
	return {
		"name": "my_asset",
		"category": "prop",
		"assembly": asset,
		"triangle_budget": 4000,
		"topology_budget": {"rendered_triangles": 4000, "unique_triangles": 3000},
		"quality_profile": "runtime",
		"checks": [],
		"anchors": {},
		"front": "+Z",
	}
```

Compile it with Godot, not Node:

```bash
godot --path . --script res://addons/polyforge/cli/polyforge_cli.gd -- \
  build res://models/my_asset.gd --param height=1.4 --out res://dist --mode both
```

Outputs are GLB, manifest JSON, self-contained review HTML/JSON, and a multi-view PNG when
the selected Godot renderer supports offscreen rendering. Every GLB is re-imported through
Godot before the build succeeds.

## Rules

- +Y is up. Declare `front` explicitly; bundled examples use +Z.
- Give every independently meaningful part a stable semantic name.
- Declare a small set of bounded primary measurements with `parameters()`; use
  `Parameters.scale()` for the canonical uniform asset size.
- Express each physical dimension against the closest measurement belonging to the same part.
- Use `p.derive(name, source, factor)` for simple ratios and `p.computed()` for multi-source values.
- Never type a coordinate that describes a relationship; calculate it from the geometry or
  dimension it must meet.
- Let the default base, per-parameter boundary, and pairwise-boundary sweep run before accepting
  an asset.
- Keep pairwise sweeps enabled so boundary interactions between two measurements are exercised.
- Add `Checks.require_axis_size()` assertions proving important dimensions reached the mesh.
- Derive anchors and attachment positions from the geometry they describe. Use
  `Attachments.surface()` when a relationship lands on an emitted host surface, and return its
  snapshot as `attachments` in the recipe.
- Keep play-size readability enabled. Treat color regions, background contrast, and typical
  feature thickness as measured outputs, not judgments made from the full-size preview. Keep
  sweep readability enabled for final validation.
- Use `--mode preserve` for movable/addressable parts, `merge` for static batching, or
  `both` when authoring and runtime needs differ.
- Add structural and semantic checks before increasing detail.
- Classify new parts across construction, role, repetition, and motion with
  `SurfaceTypes.classify()`; set `require_part_classification` for strict recipes.
- Choose rounded and swept segmentation through `TopologyBudget` at the intended play size.
  Report both rendered and unique triangle budgets; repeated components count toward rendered
  cost while sharing unique mesh storage.
- For moving assets, return a `Rig` with named bones, bindings, looped clips, and motion reports.
  Bake mechanical motion from constraints and validate fixed lengths, loop closure, and static
  keepout clearance across the complete sample set.
- For new production recipes, use `AssetIntent` with separately hashed construction and appearance
  payloads. Resolve only construction intent into `ResolvedDesign`.
- Compile geometry with stable `StyleCompiler.slot()` materials, fingerprint it, and apply an
  `AppearanceStyleBinding` afterward. Treat any geometry-hash change as a build failure.
- Route a mechanism through a specialized `SolverStage`; never silently discard an unsupported
  constraint or substitute a generic mathematical solver.
- For modular rigid assets, author typed component sockets, emit a geometry-free `AssemblyPlan`,
  and compile geometry only from a validated `SolvedAssembly`. Treat socket type, twist,
  cardinality, loop closure, connectivity, and keepout failures as owned solver diagnostics.
- Keep solver domains narrow. Rigid assemblies, mechanisms, and deformable characters share the
  `SolverStage` invocation contract, not one generic internal solver.
- Generate candidate plans without geometry. Reject or repair hard failures before ranking, and
  rank only candidates that an independent domain validator accepts.
- Express repairs as hash-bound `PlanPatch` artifacts. Enforce plan locks, whitelist operation
  kinds, bound attempts, retain complete history, and rebuild downstream artifacts.
- Never accept solver status as authority. Recompute hard constraints independently, select a plan,
  then perform the authoritative solve again before geometry compilation.
- Freeze semantic identity and mass roles in `DesignBrief`; keep them independent of exact image
  coordinates. Put structural backbone, repeated junction grammar, and asset-specific mass-share
  bands in `CohesionContract`.
- Add rigid transition geometry only through an `InterfacePlan` bound to the solved-assembly hash.
  Interface compilation may add collars, sleeves, or brackets, but must not move components.
- Measure endpoint overlap from emitted interface geometry. Point contact is not visual attachment.
- Model suspension as a separate socket-to-socket plan after rigid interfaces. It may emit tension
  members and length evidence, but it must never move solved components or silently repair geometry.
- Treat realism as domain-owned causal plausibility. Every supported mass must reach a declared
  support source through evidence-bound relations, and structural edges need visible joint geometry.
- Label reference claims as observed, functional inference, or stylistic hypothesis. Never promote
  an occluded stylistic guess into a hard rule; prefer the minimal cohesive hidden completion.
- Score mass hierarchy from the median normalized projected area across declared semantic views.
  Recipes own share bands and dominance ratios; do not install one universal aesthetic threshold.
- Pin rigid motion in `MotionContract` and bind the compiled rig to the exact geometry and contract
  hashes it consumed.
- Record stage input/output hashes with `StageRunner`. The runner owns ordering and provenance,
  never geometry, style, solver, rig, repair, or validation logic.
- When a reference image exists, identify it by SHA-256 and classify each observation as required,
  preferred, or informational in `ReferenceProfile`. Only required identity may fail the build;
  preferred coordinate and proportion drift remains evidence.
- Compare normalized semantic evidence across renderers, not pixels. Keep beauty baselines scoped
  to one pinned Godot/renderer environment.
- Declare intentional intersections with `Assembly.allow_overlap()` before enabling
  `noclip` in the recipe.
- Keep palettes, categories, density profiles, and output directories project-owned.
- Inspect all eight octant views. A correct canonical view does not prove the back and sides exist.
- Do not generate procedural geometry at game startup. Import the compiled GLB.

## Useful modules

- `core/stock.gd`: named-recipe-friendly Godot primitive factories.
- `core/mesh.gd`: lathes, extrusions, sweeps, heightfields, painting, and tagged surfaces.
- `core/assembly.gd`: names, frames, transforms, overlap declarations, and merging.
- `core/topology_budget.gd`: adaptive segment selection and rendered/unique triangle policies.
- `core/rig.gd` and `core/animation.gd`: skeleton, skin binding, and clip authoring data.
- `core/mechanical_constraints.gd`: four-bar sampling and motion-clearance validation.
- `core/canonical_artifact.gd` and `core/asset_intent.gd`: typed canonical IR and split hashes.
- `core/solver_stage.gd`, `core/four_bar_solver.gd`, and `core/rigid_assembly_solver.gd`: shared
  invocation contract with domain-specific math and diagnostics.
- `core/assembly_plan.gd`, `core/solved_assembly.gd`, and `build/assembly_compiler.gd`: isolated
  planning, solving, and geometry ownership for modular rigid assets.
- `core/plan_patch.gd`, `build/candidate_repair_stage.gd`, and `build/candidate_selector.gd`:
  explicit bounded repair, independent hard gates, and deterministic valid-only ranking.
- `core/design_brief.gd`, `core/cohesion_contract.gd`, and `core/interface_plan.gd`: semantic
  hierarchy, assembly cohesion, and connection-local geometry ownership.
- `build/rigid_interface_compiler.gd`, `quality/cohesion_validation.gd`, and
  `quality/mass_hierarchy_validation.gd`: post-solve transitions and deterministic cohesion gates.
- `core/suspension_plan.gd`, `build/suspension_compiler.gd`, and
  `quality/suspension_validation.gd`: isolated tension-member ownership and paired-length evidence.
- `core/plausibility_contract.gd` and `quality/plausibility_validation.gd`: domain-owned causal
  graphs, evidence authority, and deterministic support-path gates without a universal realism score.
- `build/stage_runner.gd` and `build/style_compiler.gd`: isolated stages and enforced style boundary.
- `quality/reference_validation.gd` and `quality/visual_evidence.gd`: reference and renderer evidence.
- `core/attachments.gd`: sampled surface frames, child bindings, and attachment drift checks.
- `quality/lint_core.gd`: structural geometry validation and budgets.
- `quality/checks.gd`: named-part relationships and intersection checks.
- `quality/readability.gd`: rendered play-size legibility metrics and category policy.
- `exporters/gltf_export.gd`: preserved/merged GLB and Godot round-trip inspection.
- `exporters/manifest_export.gd`: bounds, anchors, part names, materials, and outputs.

Inspect an existing file:

```bash
godot --path . --script res://addons/polyforge/cli/polyforge_cli.gd -- \
  inspect res://dist/my_asset.glb
```
